title: Conflict "Prevention": Acquire Locks for New Routes
summary: Conflict prevention should acquire locks when routes are created rather than first edited, covering lock timing in Create, Extend, Realign, and Reassign Route and the behavior when another user already holds the lock.

slides.title: Agenda
items: Why locks must move to route creation
Lock timing across Create, Extend, Realign, Reassign
When another user already holds the lock

slides.title: Locks are acquired at route creation, not first edit
slides.subhead: Closing the conflict window between creating a route and editing it

blocks.text: As an LRS editor, I need a lock acquired the moment I create a route, so that a concurrent editor cannot modify it before my first edit.
Create, Extend, Realign, and Reassign Route all acquire locks
Lock timing moves from first edit to route creation
Applies to the LRS Network the new route belongs to

slides.notes: Open with the conflict window today: a route exists before any lock is taken, so two editors can collide. The proposal closes that window by acquiring the lock inside the create operation itself.

slides.title: Lock timing by route operation
slides.notes: Walk the table row by row. The diagram shows the lock acquisition sequence against the LRS Network for the positive case.

slides.title: When another user already holds the lock

blocks.text: The create operation must fail fast and name the lock holder.
Expected result: creation blocked with a concurrency message
Negative case: silent Stay Put leaves the route unlocked

slides.notes: This merges the negative-case fragments from the source slides: the failure mode we must not ship is a created-but-unlocked route.

slides.title: Key takeaways
items: Locks move from first edit to route creation across all four route operations.
A held lock must block creation with a clear concurrency message.
The unlocked-after-create window is the defect this story eliminates.
Test plans must cover Create, Extend, Realign, and Reassign paths.
